n:
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “all Israel.”

*Translator's note:* Or “tore down.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “the high places and the altars from all Judah and Benjamin and in Ephraim and in Manasseh until finished.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and the sons of Israel returned, each to his possession to their cities.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and Hezekiah appointed the divisions of the priests and the Levites according to their divisions, each in accordance with his service for the priests and for the Levites.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “in the gates of the encampments of the Lord.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “the portion of the king [was].”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “festivals, as written.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and when the word spread out.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “the sons of Israel multiplied.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and the sons of Israel and Judah.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “heaps, heaps.” Repetition of the noun draws attention to the large number of heaps.
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “they began the heaps to establish.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “they blessed the Lord and his people Israel.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “tenth.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and holy things in faithfulness.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “to their brothers.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “like great, like small” (i.e., old and young alike).

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “in addition enrolling them by males from a son of three years and upwards, to everyone who enters the house of the Lord for a matter of a day in its day, for their service by their duties according to their divisions.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “the priests in the fields of the pastureland of their cities in every city and city.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “designated by names.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and in all the work which he began with regard to the service of the house of God and with respect to the law and with respect to the commandment, to seek his God; with all his heart he acted and he succeeded.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and he said to break into them for himself.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and his face was for war against Jerusalem.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and they closed up all the springs and the stream that flows in the midst of the land.” Here אָרֶץ (ʾarets, “land”) does not refer to the entire land, but to a smaller region like a district.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “land, saying.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “he”; the referent (Hezekiah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “strengthened himself and built.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and outside the wall another one.”

*Study note:* The phrase *the City of David* refers here to the fortress of Zion in Jerusalem, not to Bethlehem. See {{2 Samuel 5:7|2 Sam 5:7}}.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and he placed officers of war over the people.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “he spoke to their heart[s].”

*Translator's note:* Or perhaps, “and don’t be discouraged.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “for with us [is] a greater [one] than with him.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “With him is an arm of flesh.”

*Translator's note:* Or “people.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “servants.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “all Judah.” The words “the people of” are supplied in the translation for clarity. The Hebrew text uses the name “Judah” here by metonymy for the people of Judah.
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “On what are you trusting that [you] are living during the siege in Jerusalem.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “hand.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Is not Hezekiah misleading you to give you over to die by hunger and thirst, saying, ‘The Lord our God will rescue us from the hand of the king of Assyria’?’

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Did not he, Hezekiah, eliminate…?” This rhetorical question presupposes a positive reply (“yes, he did”) and so has been translated here as a positive statement.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “his”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “fathers” (also in vv. 14, 15), but in this context the term does not necessarily refer to Sennacherib’s ancestors, but to his predecessors on the Assyrian throne.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “hand.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “how much less.”

*Translator's note:* The verb is plural, suggesting that the preceding אֱלֹהֵיכֶם (ʾelohekhem) be translated “your gods,” rather than “your God.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “his”; the referent (Sennacherib) has been specified in the translation for clarity and for stylistic reasons.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “spoke against.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and speaking against him, saying.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Like the gods of the nations of the lands who did not rescue their people from my hand, so the god of Hezekiah will not rescue his people from my hand.”

*Translator's note:* Or “an angel.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “he”; the referent (Sennacherib) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and he returned with shame of face to his land.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and some from those who went out from him, from his inward parts.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and from the hand of all.”

*Text-critical note:* The Hebrew text reads literally, “and he led him from all around.” However, the present translation prefers the Septuagint and Vulgate reading, which suggests an original text of וַיָּנַח לָהֶם מִסָּבִיב (vayyanakh lahem missaviv, “and he gave rest to them from all around”). See 2 Chr 15:15 and 20:30.

*Translator's note:* Or perhaps, “offerings.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “lifted up in the eyes of.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “was sick to the point of dying.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and he spoke to him and a sign he gave to him.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “but not according to the benefit [given] to him did Hezekiah repay, for his heart was high, and there was anger against him and against Judah and Jerusalem.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and Hezekiah humbled himself in the height of his heart, he and the residents of Jerusalem, and the anger of the Lord did not come upon them in the days of Hezekiah.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and stalls for all beasts and beasts, and flocks for the stalls.” The repetition of בְּהֵמָה (behemah, “beast”) here indicates various kinds of livestock.
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and cities he made for himself.”
*Study note:* The phrase *the City of David* refers here to the fortress of Zion in Jerusalem, not to Bethlehem. See {{2 Samuel 5:7|2 Sam 5:7}}.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and when the envoys of the officials of Babylon, who sent to him to inquire concerning the sign which was in the land, [arrived].”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “to know all [that was] in his heart.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and the rest of the deeds of Hezekiah and his faithful acts, behold, they are written in the vision of Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet upon the scroll of the kings of Judah and Israel.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “lay down with his fathers.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and honor they did to him in his death, all Judah and the residents of Jerusalem.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “in the eyes of.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “like the abominable practices of the nations.”

*Translator's note:* The phrase כָל צְבָא הֲַשָּׁמַיִם (khol tsevaʾ hashamayim), traditionally translated “all the host of heaven,” refers to the heavenly lights, including stars and planets. In {{1 Kings 22:19|1 Kgs 22:19}} these heavenly bodies are pictured as members of the Lord’s royal court or assembly, but many other texts view them as the illegitimate objects of pagan and Israelite worship.

*Translator's note:* Or “served.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “In Jerusalem my name will be permanently.”

*Translator's note:* Or “he sacrificed his sons in the fire.” This may refer to child sacrifice, though some interpret it as a less drastic cultic practice (NEB, NASB “made his sons pass through the fire”; NIV11 “sacrificed his children in the fire”; NRSV “made his sons pass through fire”). For discussion see M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, *II Kings* (AB), 266-67.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and he set up a ritual pit, along with a conjurer.” Hebrew אוֹב (ʾov, “ritual pit”) refers to a pit used by a magician to conjure up underworld spirits. In {{1 Samuel 28:7|1 Sam 28:7}} the witch of Endor is called a בַּעֲלַת אוֹב (baʿalat ʾov, “owner of a ritual pit”). See H. Hoffner, “Second Millennium Antecedents to the Hebrew ʾÔḆ,” *JBL* 86 (1967): 385-401.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and he multiplied doing what is evil in the eyes of the Lord, angering him.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “In this house and in Jerusalem, which I chose from all the tribes of Israel, I will place my name permanently” (or perhaps “forever”).
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “I will not again make the feet of Israel wander from the land which I established for their fathers.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “misled Judah.” The words “the people of” are supplied in the translation for clarity. The Hebrew text uses the name “Judah” here by metonymy for the people of Judah.
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and they seized him with hooks.”

*Translator's note:* Or “distress.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “he”; the referent (Manasseh) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “appeased the face of the Lord his God.”

*Translator's note:* Or “greatly.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “fathers.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “him”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “he”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “was entreated by him,” or “allowed himself to be entreated by him.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “heard.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “he”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “he”; the referent (Manasseh) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

*Study note:* The phrase *the City of David* refers here to the fortress of Zion in Jerusalem, not to Bethlehem. See {{2 Samuel 5:7|2 Sam 5:7}}.
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “told Judah.” The words “the people of” are supplied in the translation for clarity. The Hebrew text uses the name “Judah” here by metonymy for the people of Judah.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and his prayer and being entreated by him, and all his sin and his unfaithfulness and the places where he built high places and set up Asherah poles and idols before he humbled himself—behold, they are written on the words of his seers.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “in the eyes of.”

*Translator's note:* Or “served.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “as Manasseh his father had humbled himself.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “for he, Amon, multiplied guilt.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and the people of the land.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “he did what was proper in the eyes of the Lord.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and walked in the ways of David his father.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and they tore down before him the altars of the Baals.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “the priests”; the qualifying adjective “pagan” has been supplied in the translation for clarity.
*Translator's note:* “In their ruins” is the marginal reading (*Qere*) of the Hebrew text.
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “to purify the land and the house.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “from Manasseh and Ephraim.” The words “the people of” are supplied in the translation for clarity. The Hebrew text uses the names “Manasseh and Ephraim” here by metonymy for the people of Manasseh and Ephraim.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “all Judah and Benjamin.” The words “the people of” are supplied in the translation for clarity. The Hebrew text uses the names “Judah and Benjamin” here by metonymy for the people of Judah and Benjamin.

*Text-critical note:* The Hebrew consonantal text (*Kethib*) assumes the reading, “and the residents of.” The marginal reading (*Qere*) is “and they returned.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “doer[s] of the work.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and they gave it to the doers of the work who were working in the house of the Lord to restore and to repair the house.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “of the houses that the kings of Judah had destroyed.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “[were] over the laborers and were directing every doer of work for work assignment and work assignment.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “returned still the king a word, saying.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “that was found in the house of the Lord.”
*Translator's note:* The parallel account in {{2 Kings 22:12|2 Kgs 22:12}} has the variant spelling “Achbor son of Micaiah.”

*Study note:* The implication is to seek a prophetic oracle.

*Text-critical note:* The MT reads נִתְּכָה (nittekah, “has gushed forth”) but the LXX implies נִצְתָה (nitsetah, “has been ignited”).

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “doing.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and those who [were sent by] the king.”

*Translator's note:* The parallel account in {{2 Kings 22:14|2 Kgs 22:14}} has the variant spelling “son of Tikvah, the son of Harhas.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “the keeper of the clothes.”

*Translator's note:* Or “second.” For a discussion of the possible location of this district, see M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, *II Kings* (AB), 283.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and they spoke to her like this.”

*Translator's note:* Or “burned incense.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “angering me with all the work of their hands.” The present translation assumes this refers to idols they have manufactured (note the preceding reference to “other gods”). However, it is possible that this is a general reference to their sinful practices, in which case one might translate, “angering me by all the things they do.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Therefore, behold, I am gathering you to your fathers, and you will be gathered to your tomb in peace.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and the king sent and gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.”

*Text-critical note:* This assumes an emendation to עַמּוּדוֹ (ʿammudo), see 23:13. The MT reads “at his place.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “cut,” that is, “made” or “agreed to.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “walk after.”

*Translator's note:* Or “soul.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “words.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and he caused to stand everyone who was found in Jerusalem and Benjamin.”

*Translator's note:* Or “caused, forced.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “All his days.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and stand in the sanctuary by the divisions of the house of the fathers for your brothers, the sons of the people, and a division of the house of a father for the Levites.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “to do,” here to celebrate Passover.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and Josiah supplied for the sons of the people sheep, lambs and sons of goats, the whole for the Passover sacrifices for everyone who was found according to the number of 30,000 and 3,000 cattle. These were from the property of the king.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and they put aside the burnt offering[s] to give them to the divisions of the house of the fathers for the sons of the people to bring near to the Lord as it is written in the scroll of Moses—and the same with the cattle.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “After all this, [by] which Josiah prepared the temple.”

*Translator's note:* The word “River” is not in the Hebrew text, but has been supplied in the translation for clarity.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “he”; the referent (Neco) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “What to me and to you, king of Judah?”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Not against you, you, today, but against the house of my battle.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Stop yourself from [opposing] God who is with me and let him not destroy you.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and Josiah did not turn his face from him.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “listen to.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and his faithful acts according to what is written in the law of the Lord.”

*Translator's note:* Or “a fine.”

*Translator's note:* The Hebrew word כִּכַּר (kikkar, “circle”) refers generally to something that is round. When used of metals it can refer to a disk-shaped weight made of the metal or, by extension, to a standard unit of weight. According to the older (Babylonian) standard the “talent” weighed 130 lbs. (58.9 kg), but later this was lowered to 108.3 lbs. (49.1 kg). More recent research suggests the “light” standard talent was 67.3 lbs. (30.6 kg). Using this as the standard for calculation, the weight of the silver was 6,730 lbs. (3,060 kg).
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “his”; the referent (Jehoahaz) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “came up against him.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “to carry him away.”

*Translator's note:* Or “temple.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “in Babylon.” Repeating the proper name “Babylon” here would be redundant in contemporary English, so “there” has been used in the translation.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “As for the rest of the events of Jehoiakim, and his horrible deeds which he did and that which was found against him, look, they are written on the scroll of the kings of Israel and Judah.”

*Text-critical note:* The Hebrew text reads “eight,” but some ancient textual witnesses, as well as the parallel text in {{2 Kings 24:8|2 Kgs 24:8}}, have “eighteen.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “in the eyes of.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “sent and brought him.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and he made Zedekiah his brother king.” According to the parallel text in {{2 Kings 24:17|2 Kgs 24:17}}, Zedekiah was Jehoiachin’s uncle, not his brother. Therefore many interpreters understand אח (ʾakh) here in its less specific sense of “relative” (NEB “made his father’s brother Zedekiah king”; NASB “made his kinsman Zedekiah king”; NIV “made Jehoiachin’s uncle, Zedekiah, king”; NRSV “made his brother Zedekiah king”).

*Translator's note:* Or “made him swear an oath.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and he stiffened his neck and strengthened his heart from returning.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “like all the abominable practices of the nations.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “fathers.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and the Lord God of their fathers sent against them by the hand of his messengers, getting up early and sending.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “his words.”

*Translator's note:* All three verbal forms (“mocked,” “despised,” and “ridiculed”) are active participles in the Hebrew text, indicating continual or repeated action. They made a habit of rejecting God’s prophetic messengers.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “until the anger of the Lord went up against his people until there was no healer.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “killed with the sword.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “in the house of their sanctuary.”

*Translator's note:* Or “show compassion to.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “he”; the referent (God) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “by the mouth of Jeremiah.”

*Translator's note:* The verb may be seen as either of two homophonous roots רָצָה (ratsah) meaning “to restore” or “to accept, take pleasure in.”

*Study note:* According to Lev 25:4, the land was to remain uncultivated every seventh year. Lev 26:33-35 warns that the land would experience a succession of such sabbatical rests if the people disobeyed God, for he would send them away into exile.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “days of.”

*Study note:* Concerning the seventy years see Jer 25:11. Cyrus’ edict (see vv. 22-23) occurred about fifty years after the fall of Jerusalem in 586 b.c., which is most naturally understood as the beginning point of the “days of desolation” mentioned in v. 21. The number “seventy” is probably used in a metaphorical sense, indicating a typical lifetime and suggesting a thorough or complete judgment that would not be lifted until an entirely new generation emerged.

*Study note:* The *first year of Cyrus* would be ca. 539 b.c. Cyrus reigned in Persia from ca. 539-530 b.c.

*Study note:* See Jer 25:11; 29:10.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “by the mouth of Jeremiah.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “stirred the spirit of.” The Hebrew noun רוּחַ (ruakh, “spirit”) has a broad range of meanings (see BDB 924-26 s.v.). Here, it probably refers to (1) “mind” as the seat of mental acts (e.g., {{Exodus 28:3|Exod 28:3}}; {{Deuteronomy 34:9|Deut 34:9}}; {{Isaiah 29:24|Isa 29:24}}; {{Isaiah 40:13|40:13}}; {{Ezekiel 11:5|Ezek 11:5}}; {{Ezekiel 20:32|20:32}}; 1 Chr 28:12; cf. BDB 925 s.v. 6) or (2) “will” as the seat of volitional decisions (e.g., {{Exodus 35:5|Exod 35:5}}, {{Exodus 35:22|22}}; {{Psalm 51:12|Pss 51:12}}, {{Psalm 51:14|14}}; {{Psalm 57:8|57:8}}; 2 Chr 29:31; cf. BDB 925 s.v. 7). So also in {{Ezra 1:5|Ezra 1:5}}. The entire phrase “stirred the spirit” has been rendered as “motivated” to better reflect normal English.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “a voice.” The Hebrew noun קוֹל (qol, “voice, sound”) has a broad range of meanings, including the metonymical (cause—effect) nuance “proclamation” (e.g., {{Exodus 36:6|Exod 36:6}}; 2 Chr 24:9; 30:5; 36:22; {{Ezra 1:1|Ezra 1:1}}; {{Ezra 10:7|10:7}}; Neh 8:15). See BDB 877 s.v. 3.a.2.
